sanskrit: paraṃ sahasrād yo baddhvā hayān vedīṃ vicitya ca sahasraṃ yatra padmānāṃ kaṇvāya bharato dadau
english: He who, having bound more than a thousand horses and laid out the sacrificial altar, gave to Kaṇva a thousand lotuses of gold — that was Bharata.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ caiva mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yo 'nvakampata vai nityaṃ prajāḥ putrān ivaurasān
english: We have heard that Rāma, son of Daśaratha, also died, O Sṛñjaya — he who ever showed compassion for his subjects as for sons born of his own body.

sanskrit: vidhavā yasya viṣaye nānāthāḥ kāś canābhavan sarvasyāsīt pitṛsamo rāmo rājyaṃ yadānvaśāt
english: In whose realm no widows were left without protection — to all alike Rāma was as a father, when he ruled the kingdom.

sanskrit: kālavarṣāś ca parjanyāḥ sasyāni rasavanti ca nityaṃ subhikṣam evāsīd rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: The rain-clouds poured in their season, the crops were full of savor, and there was ever abundance of food while Rāma governed the kingdom.

sanskrit: prāṇino nāpsu majjanti nānarthe pāvako 'dahat na vyālajaṃ bhayaṃ cāsīd rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: No living being drowned in the waters, fire burned no one without cause, and there was no fear born of beasts of prey while Rāma governed the kingdom.

sanskrit: āsan varṣasahasrāṇi tathā putrasahasrikāḥ arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāḥ prajā rāme praśāsati
english: The subjects lived for thousands of years, blessed with thousands of sons, free of disease and with all their aims fulfilled, while Rāma governed.

sanskrit: nānyonyena vivādo 'bhūt strīṇām api kuto nṛṇām dharmanityāḥ prajāś cāsan rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: There was no quarrel even among women with one another — how much less among men — and the people were ever steadfast in dharma while Rāma governed the kingdom.

sanskrit: nityapuṣpaphalāś caiva pādapā nirupadravāḥ sarvā droṇadughā gāvo rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati
english: The trees bore flowers and fruit perpetually and were free of blight, and every cow yielded a droṇa-measure of milk while Rāma governed the kingdom.

sanskrit: sa caturdaśa varṣāṇi vane proṣya mahātapāḥ daśāśvamedhāñ jārūthyān ājahāra nirargalān
english: That great ascetic, having dwelt fourteen years in the forest, performed ten unrestricted horse-sacrifices, rich in jārūtha offerings.

sanskrit: śyāmo yuvā lohitākṣo mattavāraṇavikramaḥ daśa varṣasahasrāṇi rāmo rājyam akārayat
english: Dark-hued, youthful, red-eyed, with the stride of a rutting elephant, Rāma ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: bhagīrathaṃ ca rājānaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yasyendro vitate yajñe somaṃ pītvā madotkaṭaḥ
english: We have heard that King Bhagīratha too died, O Sṛñjaya — at whose far-extended sacrifice Indra, drinking the soma, grew flushed with intoxication.

sanskrit: asurāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi bahūni surasattamaḥ ajayad bāhuvīryeṇa bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ
english: The lord Pākaśāsana, foremost of the gods, by the might of his arms conquered many thousands of the asuras.

sanskrit: yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ kanyā hemavibhūṣitāḥ ījāno vitate yajñe dakṣiṇām atyakālayat
english: He who, sacrificing at his far-extended rite, gave away as priestly fee a thousand thousand maidens adorned with gold.

sanskrit: sarvā rathagatāḥ kanyā rathāḥ sarve caturyujaḥ rathe rathe śataṃ nāgāḥ padmino hemamālinaḥ
english: Every maiden was seated in a chariot, and every chariot was yoked with four horses; to each chariot a hundred elephants, lotus-marked and garlanded with gold.

sanskrit: sahasram aśvā ekaikaṃ hastinaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ gavāṃ sahasram aśve 'śve sahasraṃ gavy ajāvikam
english: A thousand horses followed behind each single elephant, a thousand cows behind each horse, and a thousand goats and sheep behind each cow.

sanskrit: upahvare nivasato yasyāṅke niṣasāda ha gaṅgā bhāgīrathī tasmād urvaśī hy abhavat purā
english: As he dwelt in seclusion, Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī once sat upon his lap; and from her, of old, Urvaśī came to be.

sanskrit: bhūridakṣiṇam ikṣvākuṃ yajamānaṃ bhagīratham trilokapathagā gaṅgā duhitṛtvam upeyuṣī
english: To Bhagīratha, scion of Ikṣvāku, the sacrificer who gave abundant fees, Gaṅgā who courses through the path of the three worlds came as a daughter.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: dilīpaṃ caivailavilaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yasya karmāṇi bhūrīṇi kathayanti dvijātayaḥ
english: We have heard that Dilīpa too, son of Ilavila, died, O Sṛñjaya — whose many deeds the twice-born recount.

sanskrit: imāṃ vai vasusaṃpannāṃ vasudhāṃ vasudhādhipaḥ dadau tasmin mahāyajñe brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: That lord of the earth, with collected mind, gave away at his great sacrifice this very earth, abounding in wealth, to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tasyeha yajamānasya yajñe yajñe purohitaḥ sahasraṃ vāraṇān haimān dakṣiṇām atyakālayat
english: As he sacrificed, at each rite his household priest gave away a thousand golden elephants as priestly fee.

sanskrit: yasya yajñe mahān āsīd yūpaḥ śrīmān hiraṇmayaḥ taṃ devāḥ karma kurvāṇāḥ śakrajyeṣṭhā upāśrayan
english: At whose sacrifice there stood a great and splendid sacrificial post of gold, which the gods, with Śakra at their head, drew near as they performed the rite.

sanskrit: caṣālo yasya sauvarṇas tasmin yūpe hiraṇmaye nanṛtur devagandharvāḥ ṣaṭsahasrāṇi saptadhā
english: Upon that golden post whose top-ring was of gold, six thousand gods and gandharvas danced in seven companies.

sanskrit: avādayat tatra vīṇāṃ madhye viśvāvasuḥ svayam sarvabhūtāny amanyanta mama vādayatīty ayam
english: There in their midst Viśvāvasu himself played upon the vīṇā, and every being believed, "It is for me that he plays."

sanskrit: etad rājño dilīpasya rājāno nānucakrire yat striyo hemasaṃpannāḥ pathi mattāḥ sma śerate
english: This of King Dilīpa other kings could not match: that women laden with gold lay sleeping at ease upon the roads.

sanskrit: rājānam ugradhanvānaṃ dilīpaṃ satyavādinam ye 'paśyan sumahātmānaṃ te 'pi svargajito narāḥ
english: Even those men who but looked upon King Dilīpa — fierce-bowed, truth-speaking, exceedingly great of soul — won heaven by it.

sanskrit: trayaḥ śabdā na jīryante dilīpasya niveśane svādhyāyaghoṣo jyāghoṣo dīyatām iti caiva hi
english: Three sounds never ceased in Dilīpa's dwelling: the chant of the Vedic recitation, the twang of the bowstring, and the cry "Let it be given!"

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: māndhātāraṃ yauvanāśvaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yaṃ devā maruto garbhaṃ pituḥ pārśvād apāharan
english: We have heard that Māndhātṛ, son of Yuvanāśva, died, O Sṛñjaya — whom the Marut gods drew forth as an embryo from his father's side.

sanskrit: saṃvṛddho yuvanāśvasya jaṭhare yo mahātmanaḥ pṛṣad ājyodbhavaḥ śrīmāṃs trilokavijayī nṛpaḥ
english: He who grew within the belly of the great-souled Yuvanāśva, born of the consecrated ghee — that splendid king, conqueror of the three worlds.

sanskrit: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitur utsaṅge śayānaṃ devarūpiṇam anyonyam abruvan devāḥ kam ayaṃ dhāsyatīti vai
english: Seeing him, godlike in form, lying upon his father's lap, the gods asked one another, "Whom shall this child suckle?"

sanskrit: mām eva dhāsyatīty evam indro abhyavapadyata māndhāteti tatas tasya nāma cakre śatakratuḥ
english: "He shall suckle from me!" — thus Indra came forward; and so Śatakratu gave him the name Māndhātṛ.

sanskrit: tatas tu payaso dhārāṃ puṣṭihetor mahātmanaḥ tasyāsye yauvanāśvasya pāṇir indrasya cāsravat
english: Then, for the nourishment of the great-souled one, the hand of Indra let a stream of milk flow into the mouth of Yuvanāśva's son.

sanskrit: taṃ piban pāṇim indrasya samām ahnā vyavardhata sa āsīd dvādaśasamo dvādaśāhena pārthiva
english: Suckling at Indra's hand, in a single day he grew by a year; in twelve days, O king, he became as one of twelve years.

sanskrit: tam iyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā ekāhnā samapadyata dharmātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ śūram indrasamaṃ yudhi
english: In a single day this whole earth submitted to him — the righteous-souled, great-souled hero, equal to Indra in battle.

sanskrit: ya āṅgāraṃ hi nṛpatiṃ maruttam asitaṃ gayam aṅgaṃ bṛhadrathaṃ caiva māndhātā samare 'jayat
english: For Māndhātṛ conquered in battle the kings Āṅgāra, Marutta, Asita, Gaya, Aṅga, and Bṛhadratha.

sanskrit: yauvanāśvo yadāṅgāraṃ samare samayodhayat visphārair dhanuṣo devā dyaur abhedīti menire
english: When the son of Yuvanāśva did battle with Āṅgāra, the gods, at the twangings of his bow, thought, "The heavens are splitting apart!"

sanskrit: yataḥ sūrya udeti sma yatra ca pratitiṣṭhati sarvaṃ tad yauvanāśvasya māndhātuḥ kṣetram ucyate
english: From where the sun rises to where it sets — all that is called the domain of Yuvanāśva's son, Māndhātṛ.

sanskrit: aśvamedhaśateneṣṭvā rājasūyaśatena ca adadād rohitān matsyān brāhmaṇebhyo mahīpatiḥ
english: Having sacrificed with a hundred horse-sacrifices and a hundred royal consecrations, that lord of the earth gave to the brāhmaṇas red-gold fish.

sanskrit: hairaṇyān yojanotsedhān āyatān daśayojanam atiriktān dvijātibhyo vyabhajann itare janāḥ
english: Of gold they were, a yojana in height and ten yojanas in length; what remained over from the twice-born, the other people shared among themselves.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: yayātiṃ nāhuṣaṃ caiva mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya ya imāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ vijitya sahasāgarām
english: We have heard that Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, also died, O Sṛñjaya — he who conquered this whole earth together with its oceans.

sanskrit: śamyāpātenābhyatīyād vedībhiś citrayan nṛpa ījānaḥ kratubhiḥ puṇyaiḥ paryagacchad vasuṃdharām
english: That king ranged across it stage by stage at each cast of the yoke-pin, adorning it with altars; sacrificing with holy rites, he traversed the whole earth.

sanskrit: iṣṭvā kratusahasreṇa vājimedhaśatena ca tarpayām āsa devendraṃ tribhiḥ kāñcanaparvataiḥ
english: Having sacrificed with a thousand rites and a hundred horse-sacrifices, he gratified the lord of the gods with three mountains of gold.

sanskrit: vyūḍhe devāsure yuddhe hatvā daiteyadānavān vyabhajat pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ yayātir nahuṣātmajaḥ
english: In the great array of the war between gods and asuras, having slain the daiteyas and dānavas, Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, apportioned the whole earth.

sanskrit: anteṣu putrān nikṣipya yadudruhyupurogamān pūruṃ rājye 'bhiṣicya sve sadāraḥ prasthito vanam
english: Having settled his sons — Yadu, Druhyu, and the rest — in the border-lands, and consecrated Pūru in his own kingdom, he set out for the forest together with his wife.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: ambarīṣaṃ ca nābhāgaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yaṃ prajā vavrire puṇyaṃ goptāraṃ nṛpasattama
english: We have heard that Ambarīṣa, son of Nābhāga, died, O Sṛñjaya — the holy one whom the subjects chose as their protector, O best of kings.

sanskrit: yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ rājñām ayuta yājinām ījāno vitate yajñe brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: He who, at his far-extended sacrifice and with collected mind, gave to the brāhmaṇas a thousand thousand kings, each of whom had performed ten thousand sacrifices.

sanskrit: naitat pūrve janāś cakrur na kariṣyanti cāpare ity ambarīṣaṃ nābhāgam anvamodanta dakṣiṇāḥ
english: "This men of old never did, nor shall any others do it hereafter" — thus the recipients of the priestly fees acclaimed Ambarīṣa, son of Nābhāga.

sanskrit: śataṃ rājasahasrāṇi śataṃ rājaśatāni ca sarve 'śvamedhair ījānās te 'bhyayur dakṣiṇāyanam
english: A hundred thousand kings and a hundred hundred kings, all having performed horse-sacrifices, attained through him the southern course of the dead.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: śaśabinduṃ caitrarathaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yasya bhāryāsahasrāṇāṃ śatam āsīn mahātmanaḥ
english: We have heard that Śaśabindu of the Caitraratha line died, O Sṛñjaya — that great-souled one who had a hundred thousand wives.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ tu sahasrāṇāṃ yasyāsañ śāśabindavaḥ hiraṇyakavacāḥ sarve sarve cottamadhanvinaḥ
english: He who had a thousand thousand sons of the line of Śaśabindu, all clad in golden armor and all supreme archers.

sanskrit: śataṃ kanyā rājaputram ekaikaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ kanyāṃ kanyāṃ śataṃ nāgā nāgaṃ nāgaṃ śataṃ rathāḥ
english: A hundred maidens followed behind each one of those princes, a hundred elephants behind each maiden, a hundred chariots behind each elephant.

sanskrit: rathaṃ rathaṃ śataṃ cāśvā deśajā hemamālinaḥ aśvam aśvaṃ śataṃ gāvo gāṃ gāṃ tadvad ajāvikam
english: A hundred horses of fine breed and garlanded with gold behind each chariot, a hundred cows behind each horse, and so too a hundred goats and sheep behind each cow.

sanskrit: etad dhanam aparyantam aśvamedhe mahāmakhe śaśabindur mahārāja brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samādiśat
english: This boundless wealth, O great king, Śaśabindu bestowed upon the brāhmaṇas at his great horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: gayam āmūrtarayasaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yaḥ sa varṣaśataṃ rājā hutaśiṣṭāśano 'bhavat
english: We have heard that Gaya, son of Amūrtarayas, died, O Sṛñjaya — that king who for a hundred years ate only what remained from the oblations.

sanskrit: yasmai vahnir varān prādāt tato vavre varān gayaḥ dadato me 'kṣayā cāstu dharme śraddhā ca vardhatām
english: To whom Agni granted boons; and Gaya then asked these boons: "May my giving be inexhaustible, and may my faith in dharma ever increase."

sanskrit: mano me ramatāṃ satye tvatprasādād dhutāśana lebhe ca kāmāṃs tān sarvān pāvakād iti naḥ śrutam
english: "May my mind delight in truth — through your grace, O eater of oblations." And he obtained all those desires from the fire-god: so have we heard.

sanskrit: darśena paurṇamāsena cāturmāsyaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ ayajat sa mahātejāḥ sahasraṃ parivatsarān
english: With the new-moon and full-moon rites and the four-monthly sacrifices, again and again, that one of great splendor sacrificed for a thousand years.

sanskrit: śataṃ gavāṃ sahasrāṇi śatam aśvaśatāni ca utthāyotthāya vai prādāt sahasraṃ parivatsarān
english: A hundred thousand cows and a hundred hundred horses he gave, rising up to give again and again, for a thousand years.

sanskrit: tarpayām āsa somena devān vittair dvijān api pitṝn svadhābhiḥ kāmaiś ca striyaḥ svāḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: He gratified the gods with soma, the twice-born with wealth, the ancestors with the svadhā offerings, and his own wives with the things they desired, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sauvarṇāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtvā daśavyāmāṃ dvirāyatām dakṣiṇām adadad rājā vājimedhamahāmakhe
english: Having fashioned an earth of gold, ten fathoms broad and twice as long, the king gave it as priestly fee at his great horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: yāvatyaḥ sikatā rājan gaṅgāyāḥ puruṣarṣabha tāvatīr eva gāḥ prādād āmūrtarayaso gayaḥ
english: As many as are the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā, O king, O bull among men — just so many cows did Gaya, son of Amūrtarayas, bestow.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: rantidevaṃ ca sāṅkṛtyaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya samyag ārādhya yaḥ śakraṃ varaṃ lebhe mahāyaśāḥ
english: We have heard that Rantideva, son of Saṃkṛti, died, O Sṛñjaya — that one of great renown who, having duly propitiated Śakra, obtained a boon.

sanskrit: annaṃ ca no bahu bhaved atithīṃś ca labhemahi śraddhā ca no mā vyagaman mā ca yāciṣma kaṃ cana
english: "May our food be abundant, may we be granted guests, may our faith never desert us, and may we never have to beg of anyone."

sanskrit: upātiṣṭhanta paśavaḥ svayaṃ taṃ saṃśitavratam grāmyāraṇyā mahātmānaṃ rantidevaṃ yaśasvinam
english: The beasts, both of the village and of the wild, came of their own accord to wait upon him — the great-souled and glorious Rantideva, firm in his vows.

sanskrit: mahānadī carmarāśer utkledāt susruve yataḥ tataś carmaṇvatīty evaṃ vikhyātā sā mahānadī
english: From the moisture seeping out of the heap of hides a great river streamed forth; and from this that great river became renowned as the Carmaṇvatī.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyo dadau niṣkān sadasi pratate nṛpaḥ tubhyaṃ tubhyaṃ niṣkam iti yatrākrośanti vai dvijāḥ sahasraṃ tubhyam ity uktvā brāhmaṇān sma prapadyate
english: In the wide-spread assembly the king gave golden niṣkas to the brāhmaṇas; and where the twice-born cried out, "A niṣka for you, for you!" he would say, "A thousand for you," and so approach the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: anvāhāryopakaraṇaṃ dravyopakaraṇaṃ ca yat ghaṭāḥ sthālyaḥ kaṭāhāś ca pātryaś ca piṭharā api na tat kiṃ cid asauvarṇaṃ rantidevasya dhīmataḥ
english: Whatever served for the monthly offering or as utensils for the rite — the pots, the cooking-vessels, the cauldrons, the dishes, and the pans — not one thing of the wise Rantideva's was other than gold.

sanskrit: sāṅkṛte rantidevasya yāṃ rātrim avasad gṛhe ālabhyanta śataṃ gāvaḥ sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ
english: On whatever night one lodged in the house of Rantideva, son of Saṃkṛti, a hundred cows and twenty thousand more were slaughtered.

sanskrit: tatra sma sūdāḥ krośanti sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ sūpabhūyiṣṭham aśnīdhvaṃ nādya māṃsaṃ yathā purā
english: There the cooks, wearing well-polished jeweled earrings, would cry out: "Eat your fill of the broth — today there is not so much meat as before!"

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya — he who was endowed with the four excellences more fully than you, and more meritorious by far than your son — then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: sagaraṃ ca mahātmānaṃ mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya aikṣvākaṃ puruṣavyāghram atimānuṣavikramam
english: We have heard that the great-souled Sagara also died, O Sṛñjaya — that tiger among men of the line of Ikṣvāku, of more than human valor.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi yaṃ yāntaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ nakṣatrarājaṃ varṣānte vyabhre jyotirgaṇā iva
english: Sixty thousand sons followed behind him as he went, like the hosts of stars trailing the moon, lord of the constellations, in a cloudless sky at the season's end.
